courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: Now we could use the template-driven approach again to handle this form
but I also want to show the reactive forms approach which allows us to create our form programmatically
in Typescript and then connect it to our template here.
So for that, I'll go to my Typescript file
but first of all, we need to enable that reactive forms approach and hence, we need to go to the module
that includes our new offers page which is the new offers page module
and there, we can remove the forms module from @angular/forms and instead, import the reactive forms module
and add this to our imports here
and this unlocks all the features we need in the new offer page to use the reactive forms approach.
Now in there, we can create a form property which will be of type form group and form group needs to be
imported from @angular/forms.
Now this form here should be created in ngOnInit,
so we'll set this form equal to new form group,
that is how you create a new form programmatically in Angular. Now form group takes a Javascript object
where we configure it and most importantly, where we configure its controls.
So here, we assign simple key-value pairs where the key is the name of a control and the value is the
configuration of that control
and we'll need a title control,
we'll need a description control,
we'll need a price control,
we'll need a date from control and a date to control.
Later we'll also add controls for a picked location and a picked image but we'll add these features
later,
so for now, we'll stick to these simple fields.
Now each of these fields needs a value of course and the value is a new form control.
Now form control also needs to be imported from @angular/forms
and in case you're already used to working with Angular forms and reactive forms approach, of course
you could use the form builder here as well
but I like this very clear approach. So form control takes a default value which is null because I don't
want to fill this title with any default value and then an object where we can configure it and this
object here for example allows us to set when this form control should update.
So should it update onChange which is every keystroke or when the whole form is submitted or what I
want to choose here when the form input blurs,
so when it loses focus. We can also set up validators here, validators should be an array of validators
and there, you can access validators which is an object imported from @angular/forms
and that simply groups all the built-in validators Angular ships with and there for example, I'll use
the required validator.
So now just make sure that the title will be required,
you could of course also access validators minlength or anything like that
and again the Angular documentation is the place to go to learn all about that.
So here for the description, I'll also set up a form control with no default value, here I also want to
update on losing focus and I'll add my validators array where I access validators required and of course
here, you could also set a minlength or what I'll do here, add the maxlength validator,
this now has to be executed like a function and there, we pass in the maximum length we want to allow
and I want to allow no more than let's say 180 characters. Now for the price here, we create another new
form control, default value is null and in the object where we configure that control, I set update on
to blur and I then add my validators where I want to have the required validator but I also want to
make sure that we have to at least enter a price of one, so that zero or anything below one or a negative
price is not allowed
and that is possible with validators min, not minlength but just min
and then you enter your minimal number, like one and now if you would enter 0 or 0.5 or -1
or -1000 into this input field, it would not be treated as valid. Now what about date from and
to?
Well these are also new form controls which don't start with a default value,
I want to update when we lose focus and here my validators, there I'll just require this,
so it must not be empty
and as I mentioned, the good thing about Ionic is that these date time controls are really just usable
as regular form inputs,
that is pretty nice and makes working with them particularly easy.
So here, I create another new form control, starting value is null, I want to update on blur and my validator is
here,
there I got validators required. So that is the form with which I want to work for now,
the next step will be to synchronize this form object to our HTML code.
